question: What is the Financial Intelligence Authority (FIA) section on the URA portal?
answer: Hosted at https://ura.go.ug/download-category/financial-intelligence-authority/ and https://ura.go.ug/en/download/ml-tf-risk-assessment-on-tax-crimes-and-proceeds/, this section publishes strategic anti-money laundering (AML) and counter-terrorist financing (CFT) reports, risk assessments, and compliance guidelines developed jointly by URA and the Financial Intelligence Authority (FIA) of Uganda.

question: What is the ML/TF Risk Assessment on Tax Crimes and Proceeds (July 18, 2025)?
answer: Published on July 18, 2025 (3 MB PDF, 310 downloads), this comprehensive risk assessment was conducted as a national self-assessment by the authorities of the Republic of Uganda using the Domestic Tax Evasion Risk Assessment Tool developed by the World Bank Group. It evaluates the vulnerability of Uganda's financial and commercial systems to money laundering and terrorism financing predicate crimes stemming from domestic tax evasion and trade-based illicit financial flows.

question: What are the primary tax crimes identified in the National ML/TF Risk Assessment?
answer: The risk assessment identifies major high-risk tax offences generating illicit proceeds: 1) Fraudulent VAT input tax claims and fictitious invoicing networks (missing trader fraud); 2) Under-declaration of customs value and trade-based misinvoicing (TBML) at border points; 3) Concealment of corporate turnover and cash-intensive shadow economy transactions; 4) Offshore profit shifting, transfer mispricing, and unapproved management fees; 5) Real estate tax fraud and unrecorded property transfers; 6) Fuel smuggling and transit cargo dumping.

question: How do URA and the Financial Intelligence Authority (FIA) collaborate in investigations?
answer: URA and the FIA maintain institutional integration under the Anti-Money Laundering Act 2013: 1) Intelligence Sharing: The FIA disseminates financial intelligence reports (FIRs) and Suspicious Transaction Reports (STRs) to the URA Tax Investigations Department; 2) Predicate Crime Prosecution: Tax crimes are designated predicate offences to money laundering, enabling joint prosecution by URA, the Office of the Director of Public Prosecutions (ODPP), and the Criminal Investigations Directorate (CID); 3) Asset Recovery: Powers to freeze, seize, and forfeit illicit assets derived from tax evasion under the AML Act and Section 46 TPCA; 4) Financial Institution Audits: Joint compliance reviews of accountable persons (banks, forex bureaus, casinos, real estate agents) regarding customer due diligence (CDD) and large cash transaction reporting.

question: What are the mandatory AML/CFT reporting obligations for accountable persons in Uganda?
answer: Under the Anti-Money Laundering Act 2013 and Amendment Regulations 2023: 1) Customer Due Diligence (CDD): Accountable entities must identify and verify customers, beneficial owners, and politically exposed persons (PEPs), retaining records for at least 10 years; 2) Cash Transaction Reports (CTR): Mandatory reporting of single or aggregated cash transactions exceeding USD 10,000 or UGX 20,000,000; 3) Suspicious Transaction Reports (STR): Mandatory submission of STRs to the FIA within two (2) working days of forming suspicion; 4) Penalties: Failure to report attracts administrative fines up to UGX 100 million and criminal liability for compliance officers.

question: What World Bank methodology was utilized for Uganda's Domestic Tax Evasion Risk Assessment?
answer: The assessment utilized the World Bank Group Domestic Tax Evasion Risk Assessment Tool, which applies structured quantitative modules: 1) Threat Assessment: Volume, velocity, and geographic concentration of tax crimes; 2) Vulnerability Assessment: Institutional weaknesses, cash economy prevalence, cross-border porous borders, and corporate opacity; 3) Sectoral Risk Profiling: Evaluates risk across banking, mobile money, real estate, import/export, extractives, and wholesale trading sectors.
